lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: Sampling, conditioning, latent diffusion, and video generation
unit.description: Explains test-time diffusion sampling from random noise, prompt conditioning, latent diffusion for efficiency, and how video adds a temporal dimension.
unit.summary: At test time, a trained diffusion model can start from random Gaussian noise and progressively denoise it by repeatedly predicting and subtracting noise [ts=5641s]. The instructor notes that repeated diffusion calls make image generation computationally heavy, and conditioning is needed when the user wants a specific object or prompt-guided result rather than whatever the model would generate [ts=5769s]. Latent diffusion addresses cost by using an autoencoder to map images into a lower-dimensional latent space, run the noising and denoising process there, and decode back to pixels at the end [ts=5884s]. The latent representation should keep important patterns while dropping irrelevant detail, making the same diffusion idea faster and less expensive [ts=6049s]. Finally, video generation adds a temporal dimension, so the latent representation must preserve consistency across frames and can be divided into spatio-temporal patches or “cubes” used as tokens [ts=6199s].

key_points.text: Diffusion sampling starts from random Gaussian noise and progressively subtracts predicted noise until an image appears.
Vanilla diffusion has no guarantee of producing a requested object unless the generation is conditioned on a prompt or another modality.
Latent diffusion performs the same noising and denoising process in a lower-dimensional latent space produced by an encoder.
The decoder maps the recovered latent z0 back into a clean image after latent denoising.
Video generation adds a temporal dimension, so diffusion must model spatio-temporal consistency across frames.

kp_catalog.name: Diffusion sampling and conditioning
kp_catalog.description: At inference, diffusion begins from noise and repeatedly denoises; prompt or modality conditioning guides the generation toward a desired output.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Sampling and conditioning are important extensions after students understand the denoising objective.

kp_catalog.name: Latent diffusion models
kp_catalog.description: LDMs run diffusion in a compressed latent space rather than pixel space to make high-resolution generation tractable.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because latent diffusion models formalizes how lDMs run diffusion in a compressed latent space rather than pixel space to make high-resolution generation tractable, which later units use as core machinery rather than background context.
